claims.text: Thinking OFF fails on CONTENT, not format: on a short rigid-contract selection task (10 seeded variants, temperature 0), enable_thinking=false scored 3/10 exactly-correct vs 10/10 with thinking on (Fisher exact one-sided p=0.0015). On a ~24k-char log-comprehension extraction task (8 variants): 5/8 off vs 8/8 on. Combined 8/18 vs 18/18, p=0.00017.

All 36 trials in BOTH modes produced strictly parseable bare JSON meeting the output contract format. The predecessor's framing (thinking off chosen for parse convenience; failures attributed to format at 24k chars) is not reproduced: format compliance was 100% everywhere; the off-mode failures are wrong selections/counts/extractions, including internally inconsistent outputs (count field contradicting ids length).

Measured cost of thinking ON at temperature 0 on the live K6/fp8_per_channel server: mean wall 0.29s -> 4.46s (short task) and 2.88s -> 27.58s (24k task); mean completion tokens 22.5 -> 745.9 and 120.8 -> 3485.2.

Corroborating prior receipt: QWEN27_MTP_K6_OPTIMIZATION_2026-07-30.md 'Important workload boundary' independently measured enable_thinking=false reducing MTP acceptance and throughput (61.088 tok/s K6 vs 82.574+ default), so thinking off is not even a raw-throughput win per output token on prose.

artifacts: Benchmark: 10 variants short rigid-contract + 8 variants 24k-char extraction, both modes, temp 0, seeded, mechanically scored (strict/lenient JSON, exact ground-truth equality)

tests.command: python3 think_bench.py <out.json> against http://127.0.0.1:8010 (exit=0, 36/36 requests completed, 0 errors)
tests.result: off: 3/10 + 5/8 correct; on: 10/10 + 8/8; all outputs strict-JSON in both modes

decisions_requested.decision: DEFAULT DECIDED BY MEASUREMENT: enable_thinking=true is the fleet default for any correctness-bearing task. enable_thinking=false is permitted only with an explicit latency justification AND a per-task measured error tolerance, because its measured error rate here was 70% (short contract) and 37.5% (24k extraction). Requesting Hannah Prime propagate this to mechanical-queue configs that inherited the predecessor's thinking=false.

risks: Thinking ON costs ~10-15x wall latency and ~30x completion tokens on short tasks; queues sized on off-mode latency will need re-sizing.
The 24k task here is synthetic extraction; other 24k workloads may differ, but the direction (off-mode content errors) was consistent across both task shapes.
